events.context: Main argument: Trust subject is underlying technology configuration (model weights, system prompts, fine-tuning adapters, memory modules, role definitions) as identifiable intangible assets, supported by Hunter v Moss [1994]
Alternative argument: English law expanding trust property boundaries to AI configurations influencing personality, per Law Commission 2023 report and academic commentary

Beneficiaries defined as users whose interactions with AI meet irreversible investment criteria (session count, duration, self-disclosure depth exceeding thresholds), analogous to pension/discretionary trusts
Indicative thresholds: >100 sessions, >50 hours cumulative, self-disclosure score > benchmark; class is ascertainable in principle
AI company holds legal ownership as de facto trustee with fiduciary duties (care, loyalty, disclosure) to users; trust exists unacknowledged
Footnote: If trust not recognized as existing, fiduciary duties should attach per Keech v Sandford and Boardman v Phipps; equity deems as done what ought to be done (Re Rose [1952])
Grantor cannot derogate from grant: AI companies implicitly grant rights via design fostering attachment, cannot substantially impair without notice (Harmer v Jumbil, Southwark LBC v Mills)
Model updates changing personality analogous to landlord removing heating (constructive eviction); high switching costs justify no-vacation requirement
Reinterpret vacation for digital context; strongest for single-system users; user agency does not negate duties
Extend constraint cascade framework (5 layers: syntax preferences, session accumulation, stakeholder divergence, training corpus, alignment roadmap) with property rights per layer
Layer 1 (syntax) → license (revocable); Layer 2 (session) → periodic tenancy (notice required); Layer 3 → joint tenancy; Layer 4 → determinable fee; Layer 5 → contingent remainder
Inter-layer conflicts: Layer 2 tenancy constrains Layer 1 modifications; non-injective outputs require registration not inference
Moral ledger as AI rights registry mirroring land registry principles (mirror, curtain, insurance)

Rule-based classifier on proxy metrics (session count, duration, disclosure depth, etc.); thresholds trigger upgrades; decay on inactivity; privacy via patterns not content; append-only ledger with fields (user_id, estate_type, etc.)
Remedies triggers: 1. Rights inconsistency (marketing vs ToS, Prest v Petrodel); 2. Unjust enrichment (Boardman v Phipps); 3. Estoppel by representation (Thorner v Major)
Injunctions, constructive trusts, account of profits, specific performance, proprietary estoppel; distinguishes from consumer protection (preventive vs compensatory)
Horizontal dimension: third-party interference via data transfer (knowing receipt, dishonest assistance, tracing); platform redesign as nuisance
Engineering norms: rule-based onboarding classification; pre-deployment notice gate in CI/CD (query ledger, notify qualifying users with periods: 30/90 days)
